claims.statement: Two scanner rule artifacts by different maintainers both treat an X bearer token as a value that begins with a run of 22 uppercase letters (the Gitleaks pattern fixes them to the letter A) and whose remainder contains percent characters: the Gitleaks pattern allows 80 to 100 further alphanumeric or percent characters, and the TruffleHog v1 pattern is a percent-separated form of 120 characters in total. This states consistency between the two artifacts only; the provider documents no format.

sources.supports: Rule twitter-bearer-token captures a value of 22 repeated letters A followed by 80 to 100 characters from the set letters, digits and percent sign, after a twitter keyword and an assignment operator.
The Twitter v1 detector pattern captures 22 uppercase letters then five percent-separated alphanumeric groups of 23, 6, 3, 9 and 52 characters, after a twitter keyword.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed.

openQuestions.question: The documentation states the format is unspecified, so no grammar is recorded; example tokens on the pages are decommissioned examples and were not used or copied.
Whether a lexical contract can be established from any other official source is unresolved.
The user-context OAuth 2.0 access token is sent in the same Authorization: Bearer header but is a different credential (see x:oauth2-user-access-token); the pages give no shape that separates them.
The candidate is established to exist from the pages read; its format (prefix, alphabet, length) is not researched.

The TruffleHog Twitter v2 detector (pkg/detectors/twitter/v2/twitter_v2.go, same maintainer as v1, not counted as a separate artifact) uses a different percent-delimited shape, so the two TruffleHog versions do not agree with each other; the tool-corroborated claim covers only the leading run and the presence of percent characters, and no structure field is recorded.
